newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bakers arrives in Tindouf for talks with Polisario.
newsitem.headline: Bakers arrives in Tindouf for talks with Polisario.

text.p: U.N. special envoy James Baker arrived on Sunday in Tindouf, the site of the Polisario Front's rear base inside southwestern Algeria, for talks on the future of the disputed Western Sahara.

The Algerian official news agency APS said Baker would meet Polisario leader Mohamed Abdelaziz, president of the self-declared Saharan Arab Democratic Republic, which is recognised by about 70 countries.
The Algerian-backed Polisario seeks independence in the territory, a former Spanish colony claimed by, and largely controlled by, Morocco.
The dispute has gone on for more than 20 years.
Baker, who arrived from Mauritania, is on his first trip to the region since U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan appointed him his personal envoy for Western Sahara last month.
The former U.S. secretary of state has also visited Morocco and held talks with Algerian leaders in Algiers on what he terms a "fact-finding" mission.

APS said Baker would also visit refugee camps in Tindouf, home to thousands who fled years of conflict in Western Sahara before a U.N. ceasefire in September 1991 ended fighting between the Polisario and Moroccan troops.

The second part of a U.N. peace plan, a referendum to enable Saharans to decide whether the territory should be independent or integrate with Morocco, has been held up by disputes over who should be allowed to vote.
The ballot was initially planned for January 1992.
APS earlier on Sunday quoted Polisario foreign minister Bachir Mustapha Sayed as telling reporters in Tindouf that Baker faced a "great challenge" over the U.N. peace plan.
But Baker's diplomatic experience, political weight and his backing by the Security Council and international community would enable him to answer the challenge, said Mustapha Sayed.
On Saturday, Baker held what he termed "an interesting meeting" with Mauritanian President Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya, according to Mauritanian television.
Baker added: "This visit aims at carrying out a new analysis of the situation in the Western Sahara."
